bullets.title: CRWD acquires ZS for $43.9B all-stock; Q3 beats on ARR and margins
bullets.body: CrowdStrike beat Q3 with ARR $6.26B (+27% y/y, vs est $6.19B), EPS $0.34 vs $0.31, and raised FY27 revenue guide to $6.08B vs $6.01B consensus. Simultaneously announced $43.9B all-stock acquisition of Zscaler (1.135 CRWD shares/ZS share, 34% premium), creating a broader cyber platform; UBS estimates $1B revenue and $500M cost synergies. CRWD fell ~9% on deal concerns while cybersecurity sector broadly outperformed (security +1.8% vs IGV -9.4% last week).

bullets.title: NVDA: +7-9% bounce on Trump/Bessent support; stock down 32% over prior 10 sessions
bullets.body: NVDA rallied ~7-9% pre-market after Trump urged Jensen Huang to return as CEO and Treasury Secretary Bessent left the door open to his reinstatement, alleviating some overhang. The stock had fallen ~32% over 9 of the prior 10 sessions amid SEC accounting probe, Chinese spy scandal involving Huang, Singapore export control violations (~50% of intl revenue at risk), and Southeast Asia shipment halts. UBS is cutting data center revenue estimates ~10% C2027E and ~20% C2028E, flagging ~25% gap between compute build plans and powered-shell availability.

bullets.title: MRVL: UBS cuts PT from $350 to $200; slashes C2027/28 estimates on DC overbuild and LITE deal concerns
bullets.body: UBS cut MRVL C2027E revenue from $20.1B to $18.1B and C2028E from $33.1B to $26.5B on data center power/land constraints, pulling the PT from $350 to $200 at 20x C2028E EPS of $9.86. Investor feedback on the LITE acquisition has skewed negative — LITE is sold out through C2029, raising concerns about buying at peak optical scarcity at a fixed 4.5x exchange ratio. Near-term estimates held at Oct Q $3.2B/$1.10 and Jan Q $3.8B/$1.38.

bullets.title: Semis (SOX) worst week since 2011; UBS cuts DC ests, but NTM P/E near historical trough
bullets.body: SOX fell 17% last week, the worst week since September 2011; NDX down 11%, bottom 5 week in 20 years. UBS's Tim Arcuri is cutting data center revenue estimates ~10% C2027E and ~20% C2028E across coverage, citing ~51GW compute built vs ~38GW powered-shell availability in C2027. SOX NTM P/E is now only 10-15% above 2018 and post-COVID troughs, within historical range for a tactical bottom; Morgan Stanley's Wilson notes S&P at 16.4x vs fair value 19.0-19.6x with VIX hitting 36.

bullets.title: ORCL: OpenAI deal fully funded; JPM reaffirms OW on vendor financing clarity
bullets.body: Oracle confirmed its OpenAI infrastructure contract (representing ~50% of existing RPO) is fully funded via a $20B raise described as 'one and done,' with vendor financing locked across a diverse supplier base. Large AI contracts structured as cost-plus with ~35% gross margin and ~28% ROI at full ramp for a 1GW contract. Company reaffirmed guidance for positive FCF in 2H FY28 and $30B+ FCF in FY29; JPM maintains Overweight.

bullets.title: ARM: CEO Rene Haas extends contract through 2033, dismissing NVDA succession speculation
bullets.body: ARM CEO Rene Haas has extended his leadership contract through 2033 and will assume a Vice Chairman role at SoftBank, putting to rest speculation that he was being recruited to replace Jensen Huang at Nvidia. ARM shares +8.9% pre-market on the news.

bullets.title: SNOW +16% pre-market on strong fundamentals; DELL/HPE earnings this week
bullets.body: Snowflake surged ~16% pre-market on strong fundamental results. HPE reports Monday after close (est. $15B revenue, $1.34 EPS; UBS raises FY26-28 EPS 2-3% but cuts PT from $66 to $52 on sector multiple compression). DELL reports Tuesday after close (est. $49.22B revenue, $6.59 EPS).

bullets.title: META: MS cuts PT to $720 from $820 on $23B incremental capex surge; maintains OW
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley lowered its META price target to $720 from $820 after the company raised 2027 opex to $227B (+29% y/y) driven by $23B y/y incremental cloud spend, cutting MS 2027/28 EPS estimates by 13%/11% to ~$32.50 in 2028. Total non-cancelable commitments rose $105B in 3Q with ~$73B spend in 2028 and beyond. OW maintained with ~30% upside; AWS confirmed META as a notable new customer in 3Q.

bullets.title: MSFT: Citi reiterates Buy, $680 PT; Ignite 2026 highlights M365/Azure momentum, MDB migration risk
bullets.body: Citi's Ignite 2026 channel checks showed broad enterprise AI adoption across Copilot, Fabric, Foundry and Microsoft IQ, with strong E7 renewal/expansion trends. MDB faces meaningful migration pressure (one retail customer migrated 500 clusters, another 47TB of data). ServiceNow showed mixed feedback. PT $680 (40% upside) based on 23x FY29 EPS of $32.10.

bullets.title: GOOGL: AI-driven search slowdown flagged as near-term risk; Ruth Porat outlines long-term AI strategy
bullets.body: JPM's JPM Tech Sketch flags GOOGL as a 'relative short' as alt data shows Search ticking into single-digit growth, compressing the AI monetization narrative. Separately, CFO Ruth Porat outlined Alphabet's full-stack AI investment thesis across Search, YouTube, Cloud and DeepMind, noting sovereign cloud represents ~€1T in potential European economic benefits and that AlphaFold is advancing drug discovery.

bullets.title: AMZN: GS Bull-rated at $370 PT; AWS 40%+ growth in 2027/28; nearing $7.5B Decart AI acquisition
bullets.body: Goldman reiterates AMZN Buy at $370 PT, projecting AWS growth to accelerate from 39% to 40%+ in 2027/28 with commerce margin upside from automation. Separately, Amazon is nearing a $7.5B acquisition of AI startup Decart to enhance AWS Trainium chip capabilities vs Nvidia. AMZN and UBER highlighted by both GS and JPM as compelling risk/reward from current levels.

bullets.title: TXN: Cantor Fitzgerald upgrades to Overweight, raises PT to $385 (46% upside)
bullets.body: Cantor Fitzgerald upgraded Texas Instruments to Overweight from Neutral and raised its price target to $385 from $340, citing positive management meetings. TXN shares +4.7% pre-market in sympathy with the broader tech bounce.

bullets.title: DKNG: Morgan Stanley downgrades to Equal-Weight, cuts PT to $23 from $31
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley's Stephen Grambling downgraded DraftKings to Equal-Weight from Overweight and cut the price target to $23 from $31. 4Q26 tracking data shows DKNG handle down ~3% QTD and GGR down ~1%, while NFL Week 11 outcomes (favorites winning 75% of games) were unfavorable for sportsbook hold rates.

bullets.title: RBLX: JPM and Oppenheimer say GTA VI launch had minimal engagement impact; bad short
bullets.body: Roblox peak platform CCUs declined only 2% W/W to 22.6M during GTA VI launch weekend (which set a $3.79B day-one retail sales record), with US evening engagement showing the least change. JPM Tech Sketch says RBLX 'is officially a bad short and possibly a good long.' Oppenheimer raises PT to $55. Tail engagement down 19% W/W but attributed to GTA VI pull; Y/Y CCU trend worsening to -15% remains a risk alongside Senate child safety legislation (MDL 3166 hearing Jan 13 2027).

bullets.title: CRM: Citi cuts PT to $198 from $263 ahead of F3Q27 earnings; core growth sluggish
bullets.body: Citi's fieldwork ahead of CRM's upcoming earnings shows sluggish core growth, limited production AI deployments, and one partner citing meaningful Q4 pipeline degradation from competitive displacement. Agentforce/D360 growing 20%+ but off a small base. FX could be a 60-70bp incremental H2 headwind. Citi cuts PT to $198 from $263, reiterates Neutral. The BRZE-CRM deal ($47.50/share) is on track with HSR approval expected by Dec 14 and close targeted June 30, 2027.

bullets.title: MU: GS constructive on 2027 DRAM cycle; Citi raises DRAM ASP +35% but cuts NAND
bullets.body: Goldman reiterates MU Buy despite 26% OP estimate cuts, projecting DRAM pricing +32% in 2027 with HBM TAM raised to $200B/$237B for 2027/28. Citi separately raises 2027 DRAM contract ASP forecast to +35% y/y (from +23%) on ~100% HBM ASP hike and resilient server DRAM, while cutting NAND ASP growth to +25% from +45% on soft consumer demand and slowing China eSSD. JPM data shows DDR5 spot prices +84% y/y; NAND spot -15% m/m.

bullets.title: DIS: Phillip Capital downgrades to Accumulate; MS maintains OW at $138 on strong F4Q results
bullets.body: Phillip Capital downgraded Disney to Accumulate from Buy, keeping the $130 target on valuation concerns. In contrast, Morgan Stanley maintains Overweight at $138 PT, noting F4Q beat with revenue +7%, OI +10%, adj. EPS +16%, and FY27 guidance implying ~$7.60 EPS vs MSe $7.38, backed by a $9B buyback and $3B opex savings by FY29.

bullets.title: EQIX: Citi reiterates Buy as top data center pick; DLR faces Kansas City permitting delay
bullets.body: Citi maintains Buy on EQIX as its top data center pick, citing accelerating 2027 revenue growth on the 'chips have to go somewhere' AI demand framework. DLR's Astra North campus in De Soto, Kansas faces a tabled development agreement and TIF plan until a December meeting, despite being a permitted M-1 zoning use; Phase 1 is two buildings (~450KSF) with Phase 2 (999KSF) filed in October.

bullets.title: Networking/interconnect plays (ANET, CRDO, COHR, CIEN, GLW, FN, CLS) flagged bullish on DC capex surge
bullets.body: JPM raises 2026 data center capex growth forecast to +105% y/y (~$425B step-up), with 2027 at +85% and another $700B+ increase, driven by AI infrastructure operators (+180% y/y) and hyperscalers (+85%). JPM is bullish on scale-out/scale-across networking suppliers: ANET, CLS, CIEN, CSCO, COHR, GLW, CRDO, and FN. B200 GPU rental prices +10.9% m/m to $6.81/hour; B200/H100 ratio at record 2.24x.

bullets.title: PLTR: Citi flags as AI infrastructure beneficiary; JPM Tech Sketch says APP delivered exceptional moves
bullets.body: Citi's Cloud Forum positions PLTR alongside MSFT/MDB/SNOW as a beneficiary of greater AI diffusion, citing platform consolidation with MSFT as the main agentic AI platform. JPM Tech Sketch separately notes APP (AppLovin) delivered exceptional moves matching its long setup, while PLTR is seeing further consolidation in enterprise AI workflows at Microsoft Ignite.
